factsAccepted: Blended gross margin fell from 27.4% to 24.1% (-330bps) over 24 months while revenue stayed roughly flat (+1.5%) and operating expenses held flat as a percent of sales — so operating margin dropped from 6.1% to 3.2%. The deterioration is entirely a margin (price-versus-cost) phenomenon, not a volume or cost-structure problem: the same revenue is yielding far less gross profit per dollar.

Pricing governance is broken: ~60% of the 52,000 SKU price files have not been updated against vendor cost increases in 9+ months, so cost inflation is being absorbed rather than passed through, and reps override list price on ~38% of order lines with no margin floor. There is a single legacy cost-plus matrix applied uniformly across commodity, A-brand, and proprietary SKUs, with no segmentation by competitive intensity or pricing power.

E-commerce has grown to ~14% of revenue and exposes the catalog to direct price comparison with Amazon Business, Grainger, and Fastenal, increasing customer price sensitivity specifically on commodity SKUs. However, a large share of the 52,000-SKU catalog is differentiated, application-specific, or proprietary, where pricing power remains — the distributor is not distinguishing between the two when it discounts or matches.

Reps are compensated on revenue, not margin, and sales culture resists changes seen as limiting their ability to win deals. Inventory turns at 4.1x versus a top-quartile 5.5x+, indicating working capital tied up in slow SKUs, but this is a secondary efficiency issue distinct from the gross-margin leak. No data yet confirms whether the 38% override rate reflects genuine competitive necessity or reflexive discounting of deals that would close at list.
factsNeedingClarification: Margin-leak attribution: how much of the 330bps decline is stale price files (cost pass-through gap) vs. rep discounting vs. mix shift vs. e-commerce matching
SKU-level price-band dispersion: how widely the same SKU is sold across customers, and which SKUs/customers carry the deepest unjustified discounts
Customer/product-mix bridge: did the customer or product mix shift toward lower-margin commodity SKUs, or did margin on the same mix fall?
Competitive price-sensitivity by SKU category: which SKUs are genuinely price-transparent commodities vs. differentiated/proprietary items with pricing power
Rep-override outcomes: do overrides actually win/retain business, or do reps discount deals that would have closed at list?
